label: last two copy-phase outputs of short sequences (L<=7)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (100% of activation mass), near the end of the copy: the final and second-to-last output steps (to_go 0-1 hold ~94% of mass, to_go 2 adds weak activations). Activation is largest for the shortest sequences: the top activations are all L=3 at the last output step (t=5, ~10 of max 10.5), and the second-to-last step there is ~0.25-0.3 of max. Firing rate falls off sharply for L>=8 (rate 0.03 and 0.01 for L=8, 9), and it is silent on the original phase, on the delimiter, and on the first copy output. It does not depend on token identity (in_tok, out_tok and first_tok lift are all flat). Misses are mostly weak activations (<0.2 of max) two or three steps before the end; false positives are mostly long sequences (L=7).

issues: The core claims check out. On the dev split, 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase, the delimiter step never fires, and to_go 0 and 1 hold 52.1% and 41.8% of the mass. Token lift is flat. The reported test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.877, R 0.747, F1 0.807, mass recall 0.935).
The claim 'silent in the original phase' is slightly wrong. The feature fires on 4430 original-phase steps, all at t=2 (rate 0.009). Their mass is negligible.

'Activation is strongest for the shortest sequences' is misleading. Only the top single activations are L=3 at the last step. L=4 holds 46.1% of the mass, against 11.0% for L=3. In L=3, the second-to-last step holds only 2.1% of the mass, while both of the last two L=4 steps hold about 23% each. The magnitude does not simply fall as L shrinks.

There is a systematic miss class: L=5 at to_go==2. This is the third-to-last step, and it fires at 72% precision, while L=4 and L=3 at to_go 2 are almost silent (2.4% and 0%). Here the cutoff is not 'last two steps'; it depends on L.

There is a systematic false-positive class: L=7 at to_go<=1 fires only 55-67% of the time, while L<=6 fires 86-100% of the time. Digit count and token repetition do not explain which L=7 sequences fire (precision stays around 0.59-0.62 within every split I tried). The label's 'L<=7' boundary is therefore soft: L=7 is roughly a coin flip, and L=8 at to_go 1 still fires 13.6% of the time.

A predicate that adds the L=5/to_go=2 case raises test F1 from 0.807 to 0.841 and mass recall from 0.935 to 0.963. It beats the original predicate and the agent's recall_idx>=2 variant (test F1 0.827).
